source_title: Getting to Know Sister's Run and Heirloom Vineyards
newsletter_intro:
I got to taste through a full lineup from Sister’s Run and Heirloom Vineyards, and there was a lot to enjoy here. From easy weeknight bottles to a century-old-vine standout, this portfolio shows real range and a clear point of view.

Elena Brooks also has a great story behind the label name, which always makes a tasting feel a little more personal. I love when a wine comes with both character in the glass and a story that sticks.

instagram_reel.script:
I recently sat down with a full lineup from Sister’s Run, including Heirloom Vineyards, and it was such a fun tasting.

We started with a Chardonnay that was ripe and lively, then moved through GSM, Shiraz, and Cabernet. That alone tells you this team is playing with range.

Elena Brooks is the winemaker behind it all, and I love the story behind the Sister’s Run name. It came from a very real, very chaotic vintage-night moment.

Heirloom Vineyards sits a little higher up the shelf, with smaller vineyard lots and some really interesting wines in the mix. The A’Lambra Shiraz from vines pushing a hundred years old closed the tasting, and that kind of fruit always brings something special to the glass.

If you like wines with a story and a clear sense of place, this is one to read about.
instagram_reel.caption: This tasting had range for days. Easy bottles, richer styles, and one seriously special old-vine Shiraz at the end. I shared all the notes on the full post — have a read and tell me which style you’d start with.

linkedin.post:
I recently tasted through a full lineup from Sister’s Run, including the premium Heirloom Vineyards range, and the portfolio offered a strong example of how one producer can speak to different parts of the shelf without losing its identity.

The wines moved from an approachable Chardonnay into GSM, Shiraz, and Cabernet, before finishing with a century-old-vine Shiraz. That range made the tasting especially useful from a trade perspective: it showed clear differences in style, site, and price point, while still feeling cohesive.

Winemaker Elena Brooks also brings a compelling story and a clear point of view to the work. Her focus is straightforward: modern wines for the modern palate, made in a way that captures Australia rather than chasing trends.

For buyers and sellers in Ontario, that matters. The wines are positioned in styles that are already familiar to many consumers here, while still offering enough personality to stand out. It was a solid reminder that strong branding, a clear winemaking identity, and the right shelf fit can work together very well.
linkedin.quote_card: modern wines for the modern palate, made in a way that captures Australia rather than chasing a trend
